correctness.rationale: With p=k/n→0 and p log n→c<∞, time t=⌊(log n+x)/r⌋, r=−log(1−p), leads to n(1−p)^t→λ=e^(−x). For h prescribed coupons, factorial moments E(Z)_h=(n)_h[(n−k)_h/(n)_h]^t→λ^h; exact nonzero pair mean is C(n,2)[(b00+b11)^t−b00^t]→(λ²/2)(e^c−1). For c=0 this vanishes by Markov even with fixed k. For c>0, k~cn/log n, t=O(log²n), and the probability of EVERY pattern on h specified coupons in a true hypergeometric row differs multiplicatively from independent Bernoulli(p) by exp(O_h(1/k+1/(n−k))); over t rows t/k=O(log³n/n)→0. In independent columns the nonzero word collision masses s_h obey n² s2→2μ and n^h s_h→0 for every h≥3; factorial-moment graph diagrams leave only isolated pairs, yielding independent Pois(λ),Pois(μ). Uniform relative comparison transfers each fixed mixed moment to fixed-row-size model. Type I event {Z≤1,P=0}; Type II {Z=0,P=0}; these give the stated CDFs with lattice time rounding exact. This proof is for weak convergence only, not a rate.
